authority: astronomy-informed comparison and implementation guidance only; celestial mechanics creates no participant typing, readiness, recognition, system capability, governance, economic, or constitutional authority
purpose: Classify which observed astronomical motion patterns are legitimately analogous to the Tempus/Vitae/ARCnet presentation model, which are useful implementation constraints for Tempus, and which apparent correspondences must be rejected.

research_sources.name: NASA Science — Orbits and Kepler's Laws
NASA Space Place — What Is a Barycenter?

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: The Sun carries the planets, asteroids, comets, and other solar-system bodies while the solar system orbits the Milky Way.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: A stable local ARCnet frame may be transported along a larger Tempus/Vitae presentation trajectory while preserving its internal relations.
correspondence_tests.limits: ARCnet transport is information/presentation geometry, not gravity or physical galactic motion.
correspondence_tests.law: A Local Frame May Travel Through a Larger Field Without Ceasing to Be Local.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Orbiting bodies revolve about shared centers of mass; the solar-system barycenter changes with planetary configuration.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Useful mainly as a corrective: a visual center need not be a physical force center or an immovable point.
correspondence_tests.limits: Human/Identity is a sovereign semantic center, not a mass center, force source, Sun analogue, or computed barycenter.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Earth simultaneously rotates, revolves around the Sun, and undergoes slower precession/nutation; astronomical reference systems therefore require explicit time/reference conventions.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Tempus naturally supports several independent temporal coordinates instead of one master phase.
correspondence_tests.limits: Independent cycles may be co-observed but do not collapse into one destiny clock.
correspondence_tests.law: Many Cycles May Describe One Moment Without Becoming One Cause.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Planetary orbits are elliptical and orbital speed varies; equal elapsed time does not mean equal change in true orbital angle.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Circular Tempus phase rings are normalized coordinate projections only. Astronomical layers should use ephemeris-derived coordinates rather than assuming uniform angular motion where physics does not support it.
correspondence_tests.limits: The civil-day prototype may remain a uniform phase because it represents clock time, not planetary true anomaly.
correspondence_tests.law: Circular Phase Is a Coordinate Projection, Not an Orbital Claim.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Some bodies occupy stable or dynamically important integer-ratio orbital resonances, such as Io:Europa:Ganymede at approximately 4:2:1 and Pluto:Neptune at 2:3 orbital counts over the same interval.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Independent Tempus cycles can be compared for recurrence, commensurability, beat patterns, and repeated relative configurations.
correspondence_tests.limits: A resonance ratio cannot grant readiness, meaning, permission, personality, recognition, or authority.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: A planet can appear to reverse direction against the sky because the observer is moving in a different orbit; the apparent reversal is reference-frame dependent.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: A projection may reverse or loop under a changed observer/reference frame without the underlying semantic state reversing.
correspondence_tests.limits: No astronomical retrograde state may be interpreted as backward human becoming, loss of progress, or negative status.
correspondence_tests.law: Apparent Reversal May Be Frame-Relative; Becoming Does Not Run Backward.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Reference axes change slowly through precession/nutation; astronomical coordinate work therefore specifies reference systems and epochs.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Any future ephemeris-backed Tempus astronomical coordinate should record enough reference metadata to be reproducible.
correspondence_tests.limits: Reference metadata describes measurement, not participant meaning.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Solar-system bodies have physical identities and dynamical roles determined by mass, position, momentum, gravity, and history.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Assigning ARCnet systems or Vitae stations one-to-one to planets merely because a diagram looks solar-system-like.
correspondence_tests.limits: No planet owns an ARCnet system, Tree station, grade, identity type, permission, or human trait by this registry.
correspondence_tests.law: Visual Resemblance Does Not Create Correspondence.

correspondence_tests.astronomical_behavior: Physical celestial motions can have physical effects such as insolation, tides, and orbital perturbations through known mechanisms.
correspondence_tests.arcanum_analogy: Inferring that celestial geometry causes Vitae advancement, recognition, psychological state, moral status, or authority.
correspondence_tests.limits: Tempus may present factual astronomical context and optional participant-selected symbolism; it may not convert celestial configuration into judgment of the human.
correspondence_tests.law: Astronomy May Contextualize; It May Not Judge.

tempus_ephemeris_metadata_candidate.purpose: Make future astronomical context reproducible before adding symbolic interpretation.

combined_disposition: The solar-system resemblance is meaningful at the level of nested motion, independent cycles, transported frames, resonance mathematics, and reference-frame effects. It is not evidence that ARCnet or Vitae is a physical solar-system analogue, that the Human/Identity center is a Sun/barycenter, or that planets cause participant becoming.
